To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a simple neural network classifier can be trained to perform ideal binary mask based binaural speech dereverberation and separation using the interaural time differences, the interaurl level differences and the interaurl coherence of each time-frequency unit.

we proposed a supervised classification algorithm with low computational complexity for binaural noise-reduction using a simple NN classifier and a modified ideal binary masking (mIBM) target, and that the proposed method offers a 5 dB improvement in SNR on the frequency weighted SNR over unprocessed speech in the presence of reverberation.
a supervised learning based binaural speech processing system can be built using a simple NN classifier with a modified IBM as the target.

a low-complexity binaural speech processing algorithm, which can be easily implemented in hearing aids and is robust to reverberation.
a practical and efficient algorithm for binaual speech enhancement/separation with dereverberation capability, which is applicable to real-time hearing aids.
the development of binaural signal processing algorithms for speech enhancement and separation, and the proposed algorithm can potentially be used as a binaural hearing aid.

our proposed method can achieve a good balance between speech enhancement and separation performance, while being computationally efficient enough for practical implementation in a binaural hearing aid.
the proposed method is a low complexity and effective solution for binaural noise suppression and dereverbera tion in the presence of multiple speakers.
our proposed algorithm is capable of separating and dereverberating speech in the presence of noise and reverberation with good performance and low complexity.

the mIBM based supervised classification algorithm with simple NNs can be used as a practical binaural hearing aid for speech enhancement/separation, and dereverberaton.

the proposed algorithm is able to achieve a balance between the performance and the complexity.

the simple NNs can be effectively trained using a mIBM as a target, thus providing a practical solution for the challenging binaural separation and dereverb problem.

a simple NN based supervised learning algorithm can yield comparable performance to a complicated benchmark system for binaural separation and dereverbation, which is a promising approach for practical binaural hearing aid systems.
